# Security Policy

## Scope

This repository contains educational documentation (Markdown, SVG diagrams, and related assets). It does not include executable code, APIs, or backend services.

Security reports for this project are limited to:

- **Exposed secrets or credentials** accidentally committed to the repository.
- **Malicious or compromised links** embedded in the handbook, tracker, or contribution templates.
- **Supply-chain risks** in GitHub Actions workflows (e.g., pinned action versions, unexpected permissions).

## Reporting a Vulnerability

If you discover a security issue that falls within the scope above, please report it responsibly:

1. **Do not open a public issue.** Security reports should remain private until resolved.
2. **Email the maintainer directly** at the address listed in the repository owner's GitHub profile, or use [GitHub's private vulnerability reporting](https://github.com/SagarBiswas-MultiHAT/awesome-cybersecurity-paths/security/advisories/new) feature.
3. Include a clear description of the issue, the affected file(s) or link(s), and steps to reproduce if applicable.

You can expect an initial response within 72 hours. Confirmed issues will be patched promptly, and reporters will be credited in the fix commit (unless they prefer to remain anonymous).

## Responsible Disclosure

This project follows coordinated disclosure practices. Please allow a reasonable window for fixes before sharing details publicly.

## Out of Scope

- Vulnerabilities in third-party tools, platforms, or certifications referenced in the handbook.
- General feedback on content accuracy or formatting (please use [Issues](https://github.com/SagarBiswas-MultiHAT/awesome-cybersecurity-paths/issues) or [Discussions](https://github.com/SagarBiswas-MultiHAT/awesome-cybersecurity-paths/discussions) for those).

Thank you for helping keep this project and its community safe.
